PullRequest.Title: sessions: give the shared Sessions code its workbench homes (no behavior change)
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

## What

Follow-up to #346421, which moved the reusable Sessions code into `src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions` as one block. This PR gives that code its logical workbench homes, in three steps:

1. **Self-contained pieces go to their natural homes.** The diff editor options service goes to `services/editor`, `DockedEditorInput` to `browser/parts/editor`, the GitHub API client to `services/github/browser`, and the Changes editor and view to a new `contrib/sessionChanges`.
2. **The Sessions part becomes a frame plus content**, like the editor part hosts editor panes. The frame (card, sizing, activity bar host, empty-state frame, progress) goes to `browser/parts/sessions`, next to the editor, sidebar and panel parts. The session grid stays in `contrib/sessions` as `SessionsGridContent`. It plugs into the frame through `SessionsPartContentRegistry` behind the `ISessionsPartContent` contract. The host layout contract goes to `services/sessions/browser`.
3. **The session model and host routing go to `services/sessions/{common,browser}`.** The 4 chat and canvas shapes the model uses move down to `vs/workbench/common`. The session pane types are split out of `sessionsManagement`, and the chat-free session services move along.

77 files move. There are **no shims**: every importer is rewritten to the new path, including the chat and canvases importers of the moved shapes.

**No behaviour change.** The Agents window (`--agents`) and the editor window behave exactly as on `main`. There is no new setting, feature gate or exposed API.

## How it stays behaviour-neutral

- The only new registration is `SessionsPartContentRegistry.register(SessionsGridContent)`. It is made once from `vs/sessions/browser/parts/sessionsPartContent.registration.ts`, which only the Agents window entry points load. No moved code and no code in `browser/` or `services/` registers at module scope.
- The frame owns the content instance: it creates the content from the registered descriptor and disposes it with itself. The Agents window asks for the grid content by id (`agents.sessionsGrid`). An unknown id disposes the frame and throws.
- The editor window loads nothing new. Its module set changes only by the 3 split-out shape modules, which come from modules it already loads, and by 2 files that load from their new paths.
- `vs/workbench` never imports `vs/sessions`. No new two-way contrib dependency.
- Moved strings keep their localization project: the sessions homes stay in `vscode-sessions` (`build/lib/i18n.ts`, with a test).
- The eslint `_meta` guard, the `IAgentSessionsService` rule and CODENOTIFY now also cover the 3 new homes.

## Decisions

- **One PR** for all three steps, reviewed commit by commit. Prep, pure-move, symbol-move, config and docs commits are kept separate, in order step 1 → step 2 → step 3.
- **A registry, not constructor injection**, for the Sessions part content, like editor pane descriptors. The frame owns and disposes the content.
- **The content owns the grid.** The frame stays model-free.
- **Step 3 covers the session model and host routing only.** The sessions management and provider contracts stay in `contrib/sessions`.
- **No shims.** All importers are rewritten by the codemod in pure-move or symbol-move commits. The type aliases that `session.ts` already exported on `main` stay as they are.
- After #346561 (one session object per session), step 3 splits out the session pane types (`ISessionPaneTabs`, `IPaneViewState`, `ISessionPaneContent`, `shownChatOf`, `IShownChat`) into `sessionPane.ts`, and the grid pane model `sessionGridPane.ts` moves with the session host routing.
- The chat and canvas shapes go to `vs/workbench/common`. `githubApiClient` goes to `services/github/browser`, and the diff editor options service to `services/editor` without a rename.

## Reviews, performance and live testing

- **Code review: SHIP.** A separate reviewer on a different model reviewed this PR in rounds:
  - steps 1–2;
  - step 3 plus config;
  - the first rebase delta;
  - the final rebase delta: commit 9 re-authored on main's new Sessions part after #346561, the adapted step-3 symbol split, and the docs.

  Low findings were fixed in place: a blank line in `sessionsPart.css`, and the Changes move keeps its sample-data paths as they were. The new eslint rules were checked with an executed probe in each new home.
- **Performance: no regression** (re-checked after the final rebase).
  - Code read: the editor window gains only the 3 split-out shape modules. Registration counts are identical, apart from the one new content registration in the Agents window. The frame/content split adds one call per layout pass, with no new listeners, autoruns or DOM reads.
  - Startup and idle CPU: measured A/B against `main` with isolated profiles, both windows. Same within noise; startup mark counts identical.
  - Two split sessions, 10 sash resizes: layout and style recalculation counts identical. Durations are the same within noise.
- **Live A/B against `main`: no behavioural difference in any scenario run.** Both builds ran from the same snapshot with the same scripted steps, and screenshots and outputs were compared.
  - Agents window session grid: one, two and three sessions; balanced arrange; sash resize; width commands; maximize/restore; drag a session into the grid; close a slot; reload restoring the grid; focus navigation.
  - Frame: empty state; side pane show/hide; card gap; part sizes after reload; title bar; customizations widgets.
  - Moved code: the Changes view and editor; diff toggles, including the `sessions.diffEditor.wordWrap` setting; docked editors; editor part show/hide; canvases.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup and initial Sessions part rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The eager SessionsParts service creates one SessionsPart frame and one SessionsGridContent object; DOM/grid creation still occurs when the part is rendered, as before. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation was added to startup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one part/content pair and one initial placeholder SessionView per Agents window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI construction on the renderer thread; no newly introduced parallelism, queue, limiter, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module evaluation still caches the relocated modules once; the new registry holds one static descriptor and does not alter cold versus warm data caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, registration, and render paths were traced through SessionsParts, SessionsPart, SessionsPartContentRegistry, SessionsGridContent, and SessionView.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The split adds constant-cost registry lookup and wrapper allocation, but these are bounded to one per window and too small to establish a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the former SessionsPart constructor/render responsibilities are split without multiplying heavyweight views or moving external work onto startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session pane reconciliation, visibility changes, resize, and layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An update still reuses or creates SessionView slots, reconciles the internal grid, disposes removed slots, and performs one layout with the last known dimensions. The new host.requestLayout indirection has the same guard and layout cardinality as the prior inline _lastLayout check.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible grid slots/panes after reconciliation; work remains linear in effective visible pane count, matching the pre-diff behavior.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer-thread reconciliation and layout; no additional scheduling, fan-out, or concurrent work was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing slot reuse by id, grid state reuse, and SessionView visibility deduplication remain intact; no cache keys or invalidation behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after layout, setVisible, updatePanes, slot creation, disposal, and SessionView visibility guards were compared directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM/layout cost depends on pane count and chat complexity, but the diff does not increase that count or execution frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: synchronous UI work and allocation scale exactly as before, with no lost deduplication or cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session, chat, changes, canvas, agent-host, and GitHub workflows using relocated shared types/services
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changed hunks across these workflows rewrite module paths or extract unchanged interfaces/helpers; their existing provider, remote, filesystem, and network operations remain behind the same commands and service methods and are not newly invoked or moved onto a hotter path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing session/chat/file/change collections and provider requests; effective cardinality is unchanged because no loops, batching, cache access, or invocation sites changed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing provider concurrency and sequencing are unchanged; the diff adds no Promise fan-out, limiter changes, queues, or subprocess bursts.
